9.01.t: 9.1 The Arthroscopy Set — Tell Them Apart
9.01.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this telescope?"
- "A rigid rod-lens arthroscope, usually **4 mm** and **30°**, in its sheath with light cable and camera (Campbell)."
- "Rotating a 30° scope scans **three times** a 0° field; a **70°** scope sees around corners (Campbell)."

### Recognise it
- Inclination = scope axis to lens face, **0–120°**; **25° and 30°** used most (Campbell)

### 30° vs 70° scope
| (Campbell) | 30° | 70° |
|---|---|---|
| Use | routine knee and shoulder | posterior knee compartments |
| Rotation | scanning effect | large circle, central **blind area** |
| Orientation | easy | difficult |

- Field of view → **1.9 mm = 65°** · **2.7 mm = 90°** · **4.0 mm = 115°** (Campbell)

- Rotating 30° and 70° scopes: field and blind area (Campbell)
- Small-joint set: 2.7 mm scope, shavers, burr, RF probe (paper)

### Sheath, trocar, cannula
- **Sheath** (**6.0–6.2 mm**) carries scope and inflow (Campbell)
- **Blunt trocar** → fewer nerve injuries (Campbell) · lax capsule → **sharp trocar**, may score the humeral head (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Cannulas when shuttling sutures → no tangling; sealed ends → **less extravasation** (Campbell; Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Shoulder instrument set: probes, passers, graspers, cannulas (Campbell)

### Fluid — gravity vs pump
- **Lactated Ringer** → better meniscal cell survival than saline (Campbell)
- Gravity → **22 mm Hg** per foot, 3 feet ≈ **66 mm Hg** (Campbell)
- Pump → knee **40–60 mm Hg**, shoulder **40 mm Hg below systolic** (Campbell)
- **Epinephrine 1 mg/L** in the irrigant → better view, tourniquet need ↓ **50%** (Campbell)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this hooked rod?"
- "An arthroscopic **probe** — the arthroscopist's extended finger, most used after the scope (Campbell)."
- "Right-angled, tip **3–4 mm**, so it measures lesions; I palpate with its elbow, not its tip (Campbell)."

### Tell them apart
| Instrument (Campbell) | Look for | Does |
|---|---|---|
| **Probe** | blunt right-angled hook | feels cartilage, meniscus, ACL tension |
| **Basket punch** ("meniscal biter") | jaws with an **open floor**, 3–5 mm | bites; pieces drop into the joint |
| **Grasper** | toothed jaws, **ratchet** | retrieves loose bodies, holds flaps |
| **Scissors** | straight or hooked jaws | cuts meniscal fragments |
| **Knife** | hooked or end-cutting blade | cuts via a cannula |

- **Double-action** grasper holds a slippery osteochondral loose body (Campbell)

- Arthroscopic probe with rounded, blunt tip (Campbell)
- Basket punches, graspers and scissors (Campbell)

### Suture instruments
- **Suture passer** pierces tissue carrying a suture · **bird beak** retrieves it through labrum or cuff (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- **Lasso** → curved needle; **Prolene** through it shuttles FiberWire (Prof Maged Samy)
- **Knot pusher** → sliding knot (Duncan loop), then **3–4 half hitches**; not sliding → half hitches only (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)
- **One** thread in the cannula while passing, **two** while tying → no entanglement (Prof Maged Samy)

- Suture lasso and grasper pulling ACL stump sutures (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Duncan loop sliding knot tied with a knot pusher (Campbell)

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Probe feels · basket bites · grasper holds · lasso shuttles**

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this hollow blade?"
- "A motorised **shaver**: hollow sheath, rotating inner cannula, matching windows; suction draws tissue in, the blade cuts (Campbell)."
- "Tips **3–5.5 mm**; burrs for bone — acromioplasty, notch, footprint (Campbell)."

### Shaver and burr
- Tip always **in view**; opening up or lateral, away from the PCL (posterior cruciate ligament) (Campbell)
- Acromioplasty depth ≈ **5–6 mm** = acromionizer diameter (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Footprint → shaver or rasp only; acromionizer there → anchor **pulls out** (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Motorised shaver blades of different windows (Campbell)

### Radiofrequency (RF) wand
- **Monopolar** → grounding pad · **bipolar** → current between tip electrodes (Campbell)
- Risks → cartilage damage, **osteonecrosis**; notch → shaver first, RF minimised (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)
- Shoulder chondrolysis → RF, pain pumps, bioabsorbable anchors (Miller)

9.04.t: 9.4 ACL Drill Guides — The Over-the-Top Guide
9.04.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "this is used for over-the-top — what is it?"
- "The **femoral offset aimer**: its hook sits behind the lateral femoral condyle — the **over-the-top** position (Campbell)."
- "The pin enters a fixed distance in front of the hook → a **posterior wall** stays, no blowout (Campbell; Nagah)."
- "Offset = **2–3 mm + half the graft diameter** (Nagah)."

### Recognise it
- Cannulated shaft with a hook or spike; offset marked in mm, e.g. **7 mm** (Campbell)
- Over-the-top = drop-off where a probe or curette **hooks** over the posterolateral condyle (Campbell)
- Resident's ridge mistaken for it → tunnel **too anterior** (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)

- Tibial drill guide and femoral offset guide, 7 mm (Campbell)
- Over-the-top area, and graft stapled there in revision (paper)

### How it works
- Wall left = offset − half the reamer → 10 mm graft: 5 + 2 mm wall = **7 mm** offset (Nagah)
- Behind the wall → **popliteal fossa**; breach = **tunnel blowout** (Prof Maged Samy)

| Fixation (Prof Maged Samy) | Minimum posterior wall |
|---|---|
| Suspensory | ≈ **1 mm** acceptable |
| Interference screw | ≥ **2 mm**; screw compression breaks a thin wall |

- Tunnel height ≈ **40%** of the lateral notch (Handbook)
- Right knee clock → **9–10 o'clock** (Prof Maged Samy)

- Femoral footprint: resident's and bifurcate ridges, arthroscopic views (Campbell; paper)
- Femoral tunnel: quadrant method on lateral X-ray, clock face (paper; Campbell)
- Tibial footprint behind anterior horn of lateral meniscus (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)
- Tibial tunnel: percent of plateau width on CT, inclination on X-rays (paper)

### Femoral drilling routes
| Route | Guide | Tunnel / note |
|---|---|---|
| **Transtibial** | offset aimer through the tibial tunnel | vertical, **11–12 o'clock**; AP stable, rotationally unstable (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Transportal (AM)** | offset aimer via accessory medial portal | horizontal, **9–10 o'clock**; knee flexed ≈ **120°** (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Outside-in** | rear-entry guide, lateral thigh | exit **3–4 cm** above lateral epicondyle; two incisions (Campbell) |
| **All-inside** | FlipCutter retro-drill | sockets reamed **backwards**; adjustable loop → 9.6 (Campbell) |

- Graft ≈ **90° to the PCL** at 90° flexion, no notch impingement (Prof Maged Samy)

- Accessory medial portal for transportal femoral drilling (Prof Maged Samy)
- Flat-blade reamer making the femoral tunnel (Campbell)
- FlipCutter tibial socket with stepped drill sleeve (Campbell)

### Tibial guide
| Guide (Prof Maged Samy) | Pin exit | Placement |
|---|---|---|
| **Elbow aimer** | anterior to the tip | slightly posterior to target |
| **Tip aimer** | exactly at the tip | exactly at target |

- Angle **55–60°** to the plateau → enough tunnel length (Campbell)
- Exit → behind the lateral meniscus anterior horn, ≈ **7 mm anterior to the PCL** (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)
- Suspensory femur → **4 mm** drill through, reamer only **25–30 mm** (Prof Maged Samy)

### Insertion — transportal femoral tunnel
1) Shave to the true back wall; knee ≈ 120°, aimer hooked over the top (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Pin → drill → measure → ream to graft size; check the wall (Prof Maged Samy)

### "Over-the-top" — the other meanings
- Old BTB (bone–patellar tendon–bone) route → graft round the condyle in a **trough** (Campbell)
- Physis-sparing child ACL → iliotibial band **over the top** (Handbook) · revision, wall lost → **over-the-top** or suspensory (Campbell)

PITFALL — "which instrument is used for over-the-top?"
- The probe or curette only finds the point; the guide that drills from it is the **offset aimer**
- Say → "**Femoral offset aimer: hook over the top, pin a few mm anterior, posterior wall saved.**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Hook behind, pin in front, wall in between**

9.05.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "ACL interference screw and its types"
- "Headless cannulated screw **beside the graft**, wedging it against the tunnel wall → **aperture** fixation (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)."
- "Types: **metal**, **bioabsorbable** (polylactic acid), **PEEK** (polyetheretherketone), biocomposite (Nagah; Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)."
- "Femoral screw = tunnel size; tibial screw **1–2 mm larger** (Prof Maged Samy)."

### Recognise it
- Bioabsorbable → **transparent** white, green or blue · PEEK → **off-white**, opaque (Prof Maged Samy)

- PEEK screws and screws in tunnels, X-rays (Prof Maged Samy)
- Titanium, bioabsorbable and HA-coated interference screws; metal-screw MRI artefact (papers)
- Metal femoral and tibial interference screws, lateral X-ray (Prof Maged Samy)

### Types — tell them apart
| | Metal | Bioabsorbable (PLA) | PEEK |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fate | permanent | persists ≥ **2 years** (Campbell) | permanent; tell the patient |
| Pull-out | reference | comparable to metal (Campbell) | — |
| Problem | head strips at removal; **MRI artefact** (Campbell; Grassi 2016) | reaction, **tunnel widening**, fragments on removal (Campbell) | none special |
| Today | — | rarely used | standard, replaced both (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Revision → ream through PLA screws; oversized stacked screws fill defects (Campbell)

### Parts and sizes
- Femur **9 → 9** · tibia 9 → 10 or 11 (Prof Maged Samy) · Campbell → tibia at least **1 mm** larger

### How it works
- Compression at the tunnel mouth → **less graft motion**, less widening · cons → breakage, weaker by 6 weeks (Handbook)

### Indications · contraindications
| Use it | Avoid it |
|---|---|
| BTB femoral and tibial plugs (Campbell) | posterior wall **< 2 mm** → suspensory (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Tibial soft tissue after cycling (Prof Maged Samy) | open physis → no screw across it (Prof Amr Rashwan; Handbook) |
| Femoral soft tissue, wall intact (Prof Maged Samy) | soft bone → tunnel may "explode" (Campbell) |

### Insertion
1) **Nitinol** wire before the graft, else fibres are cut; graft marked at **25 mm** (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Femoral screw via accessory medial portal at the **drilling angle**, parallel to graft (Prof Maged Samy)
3) Tibia → cycle, tension at **0–20°**, screw in; extra length → back-up **staple** or screw and washer (Prof Maged Samy)

- Tension → hamstrings at 30° **≈ 80 N** vs BTB **20 N**; up to **30%** lost without cyclic preconditioning (Campbell)

- Screw over the nitinol wire, femoral tunnel (Prof Maged Samy)

### What goes wrong
- **Graft advancement** → tension lost · **suture laceration** → suture opposite the screw (Campbell)
- **Tendon laceration** → tip beyond the bone plug (Campbell)
- Screw breaks or wall **blows out** → screw-only plan fails (Prof Amr Rashwan) · failure commoner at the **tibia** → larger screw (Prof Maged Samy)

- Correct fixation versus graft pushed in by the screw (Campbell)
- Passing suture opposite the screw protects it (Campbell)
- Screw beyond the bone plug cuts the tendon (Campbell)
- Screw divergence, vertical tunnel and femoral blowout (Miller)

PITFALL — how much divergence is too much?
- Campbell → divergence > 15° → ultimate tensile load falls **50%** · Miller → > **30°** femoral, > **15°** tibial
- Say → "**Keep the screw parallel; over 15° the hold falls by half.**"

### Tunnel widening
- Suspensory → **windshield-wiper** effect · interference → synovial fluid, **polylactic acid** screws (Prof Maged Samy; Nagah)
- High-speed reaming, fluid tracking → **8 mm** tunnel became **14 mm** (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- CT tunnels → correct, not widened = **one stage** · widened = **two stages**, bone graft then ACL (Handbook; Nagah)

- Widened femoral and tibial tunnels on AP X-rays (paper)
- One-stage versus two-stage revision by tunnel status (Handbook)

PITFALL — two stages when the tunnel is wider than…?
- Nagah → **> 13 mm** · Handbook → **> 13–15 mm** · Campbell (Harner) → **> 15 mm**; outcomes did not differ (Campbell)
- Say → "**Widened over 13–15 mm or malplaced and overlapping → graft now, reconstruct later.**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Femur equal, tibia bigger, keep it parallel**

9.06.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this small plate with a loop?"
- "An **Endobutton**: titanium button flipped on the lateral femoral cortex; the graft hangs on its loop — **suspensory** fixation (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)."
- "Loop **fixed** (15, 20, 25 mm) or **adjustable** (≈ 60 mm, shortened in place) (Prof Maged Samy)."

### Tell them apart
| Device | Look for | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| **Fixed-loop button** | closed loop | slightly long → room to flip (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Adjustable loop** | sliding shortening strands | tightened to graft depth |
| **Cross-pin** | pin across socket and graft | direct (Campbell) |
| **Staple / spiked washer** | tines on tibial cortex | soft tissue to bone (Campbell) |
| **Screw post** | sutures tied round a screw | indirect (Campbell) |

- Endobutton with fixed continuous loop (Prof Maged Samy)
- Adjustable-loop button (Prof Maged Samy)
- Button on the femoral cortex: drawing and X-rays (Prof Maged Samy; paper)
- Cross-pin fixation of the femoral graft (Campbell)

### Loop length — worked example
- Tunnel **45 mm** − graft **30 mm** inside → **15 mm** loop (Prof Maged Samy)
- Flip confirmed → graft pull does not bring it down · all-inside sockets → **adjustable loop** only (Prof Maged Samy)

### Aperture vs suspensory
| | Aperture (screw) | Suspensory (button) |
|---|---|---|
| Graft motion, widening | less | more: **bungee**, **windshield wiper** (Handbook) |
| Pull-out, revision | lower | higher (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Biology | — | preserved (Handbook) |

- Children → suspensory, hardware out of the physis (Prof Amr Rashwan; Handbook)
- Immature **MPFL** → patellar anchor, graft looped round **adductor magnus**, no femoral screw (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- MPFL femoral point = **Schöttle's point**: posterior cortex line, perpendiculars at condyle junction and Blumensaat's end (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Aperture (screws) versus suspensory (buttons) graft fixation (paper)

### Other devices
- Direct → press-fit plug, screws, staples, washers, **cross-pins** · indirect → button, suture post (Campbell; Nagah)
- **Internal brace** (thin FiberTape) augments ACL repair until the graft matures (Prof Maged Samy)
- ACL avulsion → sutures over a tibial **bone bridge** · blowout → screw and washer, or lateral button (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- ACL repair with anchors, internal brace and buttons (Prof Amr Rashwan)

PITFALL — "the button failed — why?"
- Higher revision → likely button **not properly flipped** (Prof Maged Samy); may break on tensioning (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Say → "**Confirm the flip: pull the graft back and watch the sutures.**"

9.07.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this anchor?"
- "A suture anchor carries sutures into bone through its **eyelet**, fixing tendon or labrum **without a bone tunnel** (Campbell)."
- "Metal, bioabsorbable, PEEK or **all-suture**; knotted or **knotless** (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)."

### Parts
- Body (screw-in or tap-in) · eyelet · preloaded sutures · inserter with a **laser mark** (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)

- Anchor designs, and metal Bankart anchors on X-ray (papers)

### Types — tell them apart
| Anchor | Insert | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Metal** | hammered or screwed | protrudes → **anchor arthritis** (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **PEEK** | **screwed**; hammering breaks it | fails in cement (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **Bioabsorbable** | — | osteolysis, chondrolysis (Campbell; Miller) |
| **All-suture** | no rigid body | small, less osteolysis (Campbell) |
| **Knotless** | tapped to the laser mark | lateral row (Prof Maged Samy) |

### Insertion
1) Needle-localised **anchor portal** → 9.9 (Prof Maged Samy)
2) ≈ **45°** to bone — "**deadman's angle**" → resists pull-out (Prof Amr Rashwan)
3) Laser mark fully under bone; tug the sutures to confirm (Prof Maged Samy)

- Lateral row low on the cortex → no tuberosity avulsion (Prof Maged Samy)
- Single row ≈ **5 mm** lateral to cartilage (Handbook)
- Weak bone → perpendicular anchors ≥ **6 mm** apart (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Medial-row anchor with sutures in the cuff footprint (Prof Maged Samy)

### Constructs
| Construct (Prof Amr Rashwan) | Idea |
|---|---|
| **Single row** | one line of anchors → line contact |
| **Double row** | medial + lateral rows → surface contact |
| **Suture bridge** | medial sutures criss-crossed to knotless lateral anchors → cuff compressed |
| **Mason-Allen** | rip-stop stitch → resists cut-through |

- Small and medium tears → double row not routine; large → lateral row advised (Prof Maged Samy)
- Re-tear → single row at bone–tendon junction, double row at **musculotendinous junction** (Handbook)
- Bankart → ≥ **three anchors** below 3 o'clock (Campbell)
- Bony Bankart **> 25%** → open Latarjet or cannulated screws, not anchors alone (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Single-row versus double-row cuff repair (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Suture-bridge double-row repair (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Construct by tear shape and size (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Arthroscopic Bankart repair with suture anchors (Campbell)

PITFALL — cement in an old anchor hole?
- Metal anchor in cement → may hold · PEEK → does not; bone too weak → transosseous suture, no anchor (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Say → "**Weak bone: perpendicular anchors, 6 mm apart, metal if cemented.**"

9.08.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you repair a meniscus?"
- "**Inside-out** → needles via cannulas out through the skin; **outside-in** → needle from outside, Prolene shuttle (Prof Maged Samy)."
- "**All-inside** → device fired inside the knee; one part anchors behind the capsule (Prof Maged Samy)."

### Which technique where
| Site (Prof Maged Samy) | Inside-out | Outside-in | All-inside |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anterior horn | impossible | only option | impossible |
| Body | ideal | yes | — |
| Posterior horn, medial | very risky | possible with training | reserved for these |
| Posterior horn, lateral | never | unsafe, peroneal nerve | **classic indication** |

- Peripheral tear **≤ 7 mm**, **< 3 mm** displaced → heals after rasping, no sutures (Campbell)

- Three repair techniques with their devices (Prof Maged Samy)

### Inside-out
- **Zone-specific cannulas**, retractor catches needles (Campbell) · cheap, reduces a bucket handle (Prof Maged Samy)

- Inside-out sutures through cannulas, ipsilateral and contralateral portals (Campbell)

### Outside-in
- **Green IV cannula** (less trauma than grey); Prolene shuttles **FiberWire** via another portal (Prof Maged Samy)
- Lateral meniscus → mark the **posterior border of the fibula**; never enter behind it (Prof Maged Samy)

- Outside-in needle passing a suture, model (Prof Maged Samy)
- Skin line at the fibula guards the peroneal nerve (Prof Maged Samy)

### All-inside
- Anchor behind the capsule + stitch on the meniscus; no exit needles → no vessel risk (Prof Maged Samy)
- Needle stop **14 or 16 mm** → no overpenetration (Campbell)

- All-inside repair devices (Prof Maged Samy)
- All-inside repair completed, arthroscopic view (Campbell)

### Stitch and steps
| (Prof Maged Samy) | Horizontal mattress | Vertical mattress |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-out | weaker | **stronger**, more stitches |
| Best for | central tears, anti-rip | peripheral tears |

1) Freshen the tear; upper stitches flip the meniscus → later ones from **below** (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Pull-test, add where tissue lifts; with ACL → tie after graft fixation (Prof Maged Samy)

### Root repair — transtibial pull-out
- Root stitches + tibial tunnel at the anatomic site; **root guide**, not the condyle-scraping ACL guide; **4.5 mm** drill (Prof Maged Samy)
- Tied over the anterior **bone bridge** or a **washer** (Prof Maged Samy)

- Meniscal root repair, arthroscopic views (Campbell)
- Root sutures tied over a washer with the ACL (Prof Maged Samy)

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Front out-in · body in-out · back all-inside**

9.10.b:
### General
- Complications **1–4.7%**; knee infection **< 0.2%**; hemarthrosis commonest (Campbell)
- Tourniquet **< 90 min** safe · **> 90–120 min** → ischaemic muscle and nerve damage (Campbell)
- Extravasation → compartment syndrome · posterior meniscal repair → popliteal vessels at risk (Campbell)
- Meniscectomy → saphenous paraesthesia, sinus, infection, early OA (Nagah) · synovial fistula → immobilise **7–10 days** (Campbell)

### Instrument breakage
1) Close the **outflow**, keep inflow → joint distended (Campbell)
2) Limb still, fragment **in view**; search gutters, under menisci, posterior compartment (Campbell)

### ACL implants and tunnels
- Commonest error → **tunnel malposition** · commonest complication → **arthrofibrosis** (Miller)
- Anterior femoral tunnel → flexion loss (Miller)
- Adult graft **< 8 mm** usually fails; aim 8–10 mm wide · length **≥ 8 cm** workable, 9 cm comfortable (Prof Maged Samy)

- Infection < 1%; washout keeps the graft in up to **85%** (Miller)
- Before revision → exclude missed MCL, LCL, PLC, PCL (Prof Maged Samy) · CT tunnels, alignment, slope (Miller)

- Considerations before revision ACL reconstruction (Miller)

### Shoulder implants
- Cuff repaired in > **20–30°** abduction → fails with arm at side (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Over-tensioned Bankart → stiffness · missed bony Bankart → recurrence (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Deep bird beak near the inferior glenohumeral ligament → **axillary nerve** palsy (Prof Amr Rashwan)

PITFALL — "a screw broke in the joint — what now?"
- Do not chase it blindly; it drops into gutters or behind the menisci
- Say → "**Stop outflow, keep the limb still, keep it in view, retrieve it.**"

| 30° vs 70° scope? | 30° scanning, field ×3; 70° around corners, central blind area |

| Metal vs biodegradable? | equal pull-out; PLA reacts, widens tunnels; PEEK now standard |
| Screw divergence? | over 15° → ultimate tensile load falls 50% |
| Tunnel widening causes? | windshield wiper, synovial fluid, PLA screws, high-speed reaming |

| Suspensory drawback? | bungee and windshield wiper; button not properly flipped |
